definition: a small but important difference in meaning, tone or feeling
example: The translation missed an important nuance in the client's request.
exampleEs: La traducción pasó por alto un matiz importante en la solicitud del cliente.
cloze: The translation missed an important ____ in the client's request.
note: Pronounced NOO-ahns. In Spanish it is "matiz", not "nuance" with the French spelling.

definition: to make a problem or risk less serious or harmful
example: We added a backup server to mitigate the risk of downtime.
exampleEs: Añadimos un servidor de respaldo para mitigar el riesgo de caída del servicio.
cloze: We added a backup server to ____ the risk of downtime.
note: Do not confuse it with "militate". Mitigate is about reducing harm.

definition: to use something you already have in order to get a better result
example: We can leverage our existing data to train the new model.
exampleEs: Podemos aprovechar nuestros datos actuales para entrenar el nuevo modelo.
cloze: We can ____ our existing data to train the new model.
note: Very common in business English. It is a verb here, not only the noun "leverage".

definition: so strong or interesting that it persuades you or holds your attention
example: She made a compelling case for moving the launch to March.
exampleEs: Presentó un argumento convincente para mover el lanzamiento a marzo.
cloze: She made a ____ case for moving the launch to March.
note: It does not mean "compulsory". It means very convincing.

definition: being a natural and permanent part of something
example: There is an inherent risk in releasing software without testing.
exampleEs: Hay un riesgo inherente en lanzar software sin hacer pruebas.
cloze: There is an ____ risk in releasing software without testing.
note: Use the preposition "in": inherent in something.

definition: used when you think something can be supported with good reasons, though others may disagree
example: This is arguably the most important feature of the whole product.
exampleEs: Esta es, posiblemente, la función más importante de todo el producto.
cloze: This is ____ the most important feature of the whole product.
note: It usually goes before a superlative. It softens a strong claim.

definition: careful and critical examination of something
example: The new policy came under heavy scrutiny from the board.
exampleEs: La nueva política fue objeto de un escrutinio intenso por parte de la junta directiva.
cloze: The new policy came under heavy ____ from the board.
note: Uncountable noun. We say "under scrutiny", not "in scrutiny".

definition: a situation where you accept less of one good thing in order to get more of another
example: There is always a trade-off between speed and quality.
exampleEs: Siempre hay un equilibrio entre velocidad y calidad, y ganar en uno implica perder en el otro.
cloze: There is always a ____ between speed and quality.
note: We say "a trade-off between X and Y". It is not exactly "intercambio".

definition: never having happened or existed before
example: The company saw unprecedented growth, far beyond anything in its previous history.
exampleEs: La empresa tuvo un crecimiento sin precedentes, muy superior a todo lo ocurrido en su historia.
cloze: The company saw ____ growth, far beyond anything in its previous history.
note: Stress: un-PRESS-uh-den-tid.

definition: the set of reasons behind a decision or plan
example: Could you explain the rationale behind this change?
exampleEs: ¿Podrías explicar el fundamento detrás de este cambio?
cloze: Could you explain the ____ behind this change?
note: Pronounced rash-uh-NAL. Do not confuse with "rational" (adjective).

definition: able to work or succeed in practice
example: Is this a viable option given our current budget?
exampleEs: ¿Es esta una opción viable con nuestro presupuesto actual?
cloze: Is this a ____ option given our current budget?
note: Spanish "viable" is very similar, so this one is easy to remember.

definition: a serious attempt to do something, often something difficult
example: Building a startup is a risky but rewarding endeavor.
exampleEs: Crear una startup es una empresa arriesgada pero gratificante.
cloze: Building a startup is a risky but rewarding ____.
note: US spelling is endeavor, UK is endeavour. It can also be a verb: to endeavor to do something.

definition: to fail to notice or consider something
example: I think we overlooked a critical bug in the login flow.
exampleEs: Creo que pasamos por alto un error crítico en el flujo de inicio de sesión.
cloze: I think we ____ a critical bug in the login flow.
note: It can also mean "to have a view of" (a room that overlooks the sea). Do not confuse it with "oversee".

definition: to weaken something gradually, especially trust or confidence
example: Constant changes in the plan can undermine the team's confidence.
exampleEs: Los cambios constantes en el plan pueden socavar la confianza del equipo.
cloze: Constant changes in the plan can ____ the team's confidence.
note: Not related to "underline". It is a negative verb.

definition: to communicate an idea, feeling or message clearly
example: I struggled to convey my idea in English during the meeting.
exampleEs: Me costó transmitir mi idea en inglés durante la reunión.
cloze: I struggled to ____ my idea in English during the meeting.
note: Say "convey a message", not "convey about a message". No preposition is needed after it.

definition: a difference between two things that should be the same
example: We found a discrepancy between the report and the raw data.
exampleEs: Encontramos una discrepancia entre el informe y los datos originales.
cloze: We found a ____ between the report and the raw data.
note: Say "a discrepancy between A and B". The plural is discrepancies.

definition: to provide evidence that proves a claim is true
example: You need data to substantiate that claim.
exampleEs: Necesitas datos para fundamentar esa afirmación.
cloze: You need data to ____ that claim.
note: Formal. In meetings you can say "back up" instead.

definition: to express an idea or feeling clearly in words
example: It is hard to articulate why this design feels wrong.
exampleEs: Es difícil expresar con claridad por qué este diseño se siente mal.
cloze: It is hard to ____ why this design feels wrong.
note: As a verb it ends in a long "ate" sound (-ayt). As an adjective (well-spoken) it ends in -let.

definition: to make a process simpler and more efficient
example: We want to streamline the approval process and cut it from ten steps to three.
exampleEs: Queremos agilizar el proceso de aprobación y reducirlo de diez pasos a tres.
cloze: We want to ____ the approval process and cut it from ten steps to three.
note: It sounds positive in business talk: it means removing unnecessary steps.

definition: extremely important because other things depend on it
example: Her feedback was pivotal in shaping the final design.
exampleEs: Sus comentarios fueron decisivos para dar forma al diseño final.
cloze: Her feedback was ____ in shaping the final design.
note: Use "pivotal in" or "pivotal to". It comes from the noun "pivot".

definition: strong and able to work well even under difficult conditions
example: We need a more robust testing process before each release.
exampleEs: Necesitamos un proceso de pruebas más robusto antes de cada lanzamiento.
cloze: We need a more ____ testing process before each release.
note: Pronounced roh-BUST, with stress on the second syllable.

definition: having more than one possible meaning, so not clear
example: The instructions were ambiguous, so we asked for clarification.
exampleEs: Las instrucciones eran ambiguas, así que pedimos una aclaración.
cloze: The instructions were ____, so we asked for clarification.
note: Spelled with "-uous", not "-ous" alone: ambiguous.

definition: to make a bad situation or problem worse
example: Adding more people to the project will only exacerbate the delays.
exampleEs: Añadir más gente al proyecto solo agravará los retrasos.
cloze: Adding more people to the project will only ____ the delays.
note: The "x" sounds like "gz": ig-ZAS-er-bayt.

definition: to encourage something good to develop
example: Good managers foster a culture of trust and open feedback.
exampleEs: Los buenos gerentes fomentan una cultura de confianza y retroalimentación abierta.
cloze: Good managers ____ a culture of trust and open feedback.
note: It can also be an adjective in "foster family", but here it is a verb.

definition: to be a good enough reason for something
example: The results do not warrant such a large investment.
exampleEs: Los resultados no justifican una inversión tan grande.
cloze: The results do not ____ such a large investment.
note: Not the same as "guarantee". Here it means "justify".

definition: to say firmly that something is true, especially in an argument
example: Some researchers contend that sleep matters more than diet.
exampleEs: Algunos investigadores sostienen que dormir importa más que la dieta.
cloze: Some researchers ____ that sleep matters more than diet.
note: "Contend that" means to claim. "Contend with" means to deal with something difficult.

definition: dealing with problems in a practical and realistic way
example: Let's take a pragmatic approach and ship the simple version first.
exampleEs: Tomemos un enfoque pragmático y lancemos primero la versión sencilla.
cloze: Let's take a ____ approach and ship the simple version first.
note: Spanish "pragmático" is a close match.

definition: a point in a process where things slow down because capacity is limited
example: Manual code review has become a bottleneck for the whole team.
exampleEs: La revisión manual de código se ha convertido en un cuello de botella para todo el equipo.
cloze: Manual code review has become a ____ for the whole team.
note: Use "a bottleneck in the process" and "a bottleneck for the team".

definition: a person or group with an interest in a project or business, or affected by it
example: We need to keep all stakeholders informed about the timeline.
exampleEs: Tenemos que mantener informadas a todas las partes interesadas sobre el cronograma.
cloze: We need to keep all ____ informed about the timeline.
note: Not the same as "shareholder", who owns shares.

definition: to admit that something is true or that you were wrong, often unwillingly
example: I have to concede that your approach was faster than mine.
exampleEs: Tengo que admitir que tu enfoque fue más rápido que el mío.
cloze: I have to ____ that your approach was faster than mine.
note: Stress on the second syllable: kun-SEED. It is not "conceive".

definition: to find a way for two different ideas or facts to exist together
example: It is hard to reconcile these two sets of numbers because they contradict each other.
exampleEs: Es difícil conciliar estos dos conjuntos de cifras porque se contradicen.
cloze: It is hard to ____ these two sets of numbers because they contradict each other.
note: In finance, "reconcile" also means to make two sets of records match.

definition: to give support to a statement by providing more evidence
example: A second study corroborates these findings.
exampleEs: Un segundo estudio corrobora estos hallazgos.
cloze: A second study ____ these findings.
note: The headword is "corroborate"; the sentence uses the third-person form "corroborates". Note the double r and the stress: kuh-ROB-uh-rayt.

definition: taking action early instead of waiting for problems to happen
example: Being proactive means flagging risks before they become issues.
exampleEs: Ser proactivo significa señalar los riesgos antes de que se conviertan en problemas.
cloze: Being ____ means flagging risks before they become issues.
note: Careful: "reactive" is a good distractor in life but wrong here. Say "proactive about" something.

definition: to describe or show the exact limits or details of something
example: The contract clearly delineates each team's responsibilities.
exampleEs: El contrato delimita claramente las responsabilidades de cada equipo.
cloze: The contract clearly ____ each team's responsibilities.
note: Formal word. In casual speech use "define" or "spell out".

definition: to make it harder for something to happen or progress
example: Slow internet can seriously impede remote collaboration.
exampleEs: Un internet lento puede obstaculizar seriamente la colaboración remota.
cloze: Slow internet can seriously ____ remote collaboration.
note: The noun is "impediment". Do not confuse it with "impeach".

definition: to reach a final or highest point after a long process
example: Months of testing will culminate in the public release next week.
exampleEs: Meses de pruebas culminarán en el lanzamiento público de la próxima semana.
cloze: Months of testing will ____ in the public release next week.
note: Use the preposition "in": culminate in something.

definition: a complicated or unexpected result of an action or decision
example: Changing the database schema has serious ramifications for every service.
exampleEs: Cambiar el esquema de la base de datos tiene consecuencias serias para cada servicio.
cloze: Changing the database schema has serious ____ for every service.
note: Usually plural: "the ramifications of a decision" or "ramifications for" a team.

definition: something that must exist or happen before something else can happen
example: Basic Python is a prerequisite for this machine learning course.
exampleEs: Python básico es un requisito previo para este curso de aprendizaje automático.
cloze: Basic Python is a ____ for this machine learning course.
note: Say "a prerequisite for something". Spelling: pre-requisite, with no "e" in the middle.

definition: logical, clear and easy to follow because the parts fit together well
example: Her presentation was clear and coherent from start to finish.
exampleEs: Su presentación fue clara y coherente de principio a fin.
cloze: Her presentation was clear and ____ from start to finish.
note: It focuses on logic and clarity: ideas that fit together.

definition: possible to do, especially in practice
example: Is it feasible to finish the migration before the audit?
exampleEs: ¿Es factible terminar la migración antes de la auditoría?
cloze: Is it ____ to finish the migration before the audit?
note: Do not confuse with "possible". Feasible suggests it can realistically be done with the resources you have.

definition: to give more details about something you have said
example: Could you elaborate on how the pricing model works?
exampleEs: ¿Podrías dar más detalles sobre cómo funciona el modelo de precios?
cloze: Could you ____ on how the pricing model works?
note: As a verb it takes "on": elaborate on something. As an adjective (complex) it sounds different (-ut).

definition: to officially give time, money or resources for a particular purpose
example: We allocated more budget to security this quarter.
exampleEs: Asignamos más presupuesto a seguridad este trimestre.
cloze: We ____ more budget to security this quarter.
note: Say "allocate X to Y". The noun is "allocation".

definition: to make a process happen faster
example: The release is late, so can we expedite the security review and finish it sooner?
exampleEs: El lanzamiento va tarde, así que ¿podemos agilizar la revisión de seguridad y terminarla antes?
cloze: The release is late, so can we ____ the security review and finish it sooner?
note: Formal business word. It is not related to "expedition" in meaning, though both come from the same root.

definition: seeming reasonable and likely to be true
example: That is a plausible explanation for the sudden drop in users.
exampleEs: Esa es una explicación plausible de la caída repentina de usuarios.
cloze: That is a ____ explanation for the sudden drop in users.
note: "Plausible" means it sounds believable, but it may not be true.

definition: being an essential part of something
example: Code review is integral to how our team works, and we never skip it.
exampleEs: La revisión de código es parte esencial de cómo trabaja nuestro equipo, y nunca la omitimos.
cloze: Code review is ____ to how our team works, and we never skip it.
note: Use "integral to" something. Stress: IN-tuh-gruhl.

definition: causing harm or damage
example: Working late every night is detrimental to your health, so doctors advise against it.
exampleEs: Trabajar hasta tarde todas las noches es perjudicial para tu salud, por eso los médicos lo desaconsejan.
cloze: Working late every night is ____ to your health, so doctors advise against it.
note: Use "detrimental to" something.

definition: to make something larger or better by adding to it
example: We use AI tools to augment human reviewers, not replace them.
exampleEs: Usamos herramientas de IA para complementar a los revisores humanos, no para reemplazarlos.
cloze: We use AI tools to ____ human reviewers, not replace them.
note: Familiar from "augmented reality" and "augmented intelligence".

definition: to reduce or limit something, especially suddenly
example: The company had to curtail spending after the funding round fell through.
exampleEs: La empresa tuvo que reducir el gasto después de que fracasó la ronda de financiamiento.
cloze: The company had to ____ spending after the funding round fell through.
note: It sounds like "cur-TAYL". It has nothing to do with animal tails in modern use.

definition: very careful and paying great attention to every detail
example: Pharma work needs meticulous documentation of every step.
exampleEs: El trabajo en farmacéutica requiere una documentación meticulosa de cada paso.
cloze: Pharma work needs ____ documentation of every step.
note: Spanish "meticuloso" is very similar, so reuse it.

definition: able to recover quickly after difficulties or failures
example: Resilient teams learn from failure and keep moving forward.
exampleEs: Los equipos resilientes aprenden del fracaso y siguen avanzando.
cloze: ____ teams learn from failure and keep moving forward.
note: The noun is "resilience". The answer is capitalized because it begins the sentence.

definition: able to grow to handle more work or users without breaking
example: We need a scalable architecture that can handle a million users without crashing.
exampleEs: Necesitamos una arquitectura escalable que pueda manejar un millón de usuarios sin fallar.
cloze: We need a ____ architecture that can handle a million users without crashing.
note: The verb is "scale" and the noun is "scalability".

definition: a hidden danger or a common mistake that is easy to make
example: One common pitfall is estimating tasks without talking to the developers.
exampleEs: Un error común es estimar tareas sin hablar con los desarrolladores.
cloze: One common ____ is estimating tasks without talking to the developers.
note: Usually followed by "of": the pitfalls of remote work.

definition: most noticeable or most important
example: Let me summarize the salient points of the report.
exampleEs: Permítanme resumir los puntos más destacados del informe.
cloze: Let me summarize the ____ points of the report.
note: Pronounced SAY-lee-ent. Useful when summarizing in meetings.

definition: clear enough to be seen or measured in a real way
example: We need tangible results, not just promises.
exampleEs: Necesitamos resultados tangibles, no solo promesas.
cloze: We need ____ results, not just promises.
note: Opposite: intangible. Both are common in business.

definition: having many small parts that are closely connected, so complicated
example: The intricate network of dependencies makes updates risky.
exampleEs: La intrincada red de dependencias hace que las actualizaciones sean riesgosas.
cloze: The ____ network of dependencies makes updates risky.
note: It means complex in a detailed way, not just "difficult".

definition: to make someone decide not to do something
example: High prices may deter customers from signing up.
exampleEs: Los precios altos pueden disuadir a los clientes de registrarse.
cloze: High prices may ____ customers from signing up.
note: Pattern: deter someone from doing something. The noun is "deterrent".

definition: to prove that a statement or idea is wrong
example: The new data refutes the claim that users prefer longer videos.
exampleEs: Los nuevos datos refutan la afirmación de que los usuarios prefieren videos más largos.
cloze: The new data ____ the claim that users prefer longer videos.
note: It means to prove wrong, not just to say no. For simply saying no, use "deny".

definition: to publicly support an idea or plan
example: I strongly advocate using feature flags for every release.
exampleEs: Yo defiendo firmemente usar feature flags en cada lanzamiento.
cloze: I strongly ____ using feature flags for every release.
note: As a verb, it ends with a long "ate" sound. As a noun (a supporter), it ends with a short sound. Pattern: advocate doing something.

definition: at the same time
example: The two migrations will run concurrently to save time.
exampleEs: Las dos migraciones se ejecutarán simultáneamente para ahorrar tiempo.
cloze: The two migrations will run ____ to save time.
note: Common in tech: concurrent processes. Not "currently", which means "now".

definition: a big and often unfair difference between two things
example: There is a large disparity in pay between the two teams.
exampleEs: Hay una gran disparidad salarial entre los dos equipos.
cloze: There is a large ____ in pay between the two teams.
note: Say "a disparity in pay" or "a disparity between A and B".

definition: to support something and make it strong, usually as its basis
example: Strong research underpins every decision we make.
exampleEs: Una investigación sólida sustenta cada decisión que tomamos.
cloze: Strong research ____ every decision we make.
note: Careful: underpin supports, while "undermine" weakens. They look similar but have opposite effects.

definition: seeming to be everywhere at the same time
example: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in the workplace, and you see them on every desk.
exampleEs: Los smartphones se han vuelto omnipresentes en el lugar de trabajo, y se ven en cada escritorio.
cloze: Smartphones have become ____ in the workplace, and you see them on every desk.
note: Pronounced yoo-BIK-wih-tus. Common in tech writing.

definition: directly related to the subject you are discussing
example: That is a pertinent question, so let me explain.
exampleEs: Esa es una pregunta pertinente, así que permíteme explicarlo.
cloze: That is a ____ question, so let me explain.
note: Use "pertinent to" something. Slightly more formal than "relevant".

definition: extremely important and needing immediate attention
example: It is imperative that we fix this security hole today.
exampleEs: Es imprescindible que arreglemos esta brecha de seguridad hoy.
cloze: It is ____ that we fix this security hole today.
note: Pattern: "It is imperative that we fix" uses the base verb, without -s. Also: "imperative to do".

definition: just beginning to develop
example: This is still a nascent market, so the rules are unclear.
exampleEs: Este todavía es un mercado naciente, así que las reglas no están claras.
cloze: This is still a ____ market, so the rules are unclear.
note: Pronounced NAY-sunt. Often used for startups and new tech fields.

definition: an official order or authority to do something
example: The new regulation gives the agency a clear mandate to inspect factories.
exampleEs: La nueva regulación le da a la agencia un mandato claro para inspeccionar fábricas.
cloze: The new regulation gives the agency a clear ____ to inspect factories.
note: It is also a verb: the law mandates that companies report data.

definition: to say something again to make it clear
example: I want to reiterate that the deadline cannot move.
exampleEs: Quiero reiterar que la fecha límite no puede cambiar.
cloze: I want to ____ that the deadline cannot move.
note: Useful in meetings to stress a key point. Stress: ree-IT-uh-rayt.

definition: to find or identify exactly what or where something is
example: We still cannot pinpoint the exact line that causes the memory leak.
exampleEs: Todavía no podemos identificar con precisión la línea exacta que causa la fuga de memoria.
cloze: We still cannot ____ the exact line that causes the memory leak.
note: Stronger than "find": it means to locate something precisely.

definition: to make pain, stress or a problem less severe
example: Automating reports should alleviate the pressure on the analysts.
exampleEs: Automatizar los informes debería aliviar la presión sobre los analistas.
cloze: Automating reports should ____ the pressure on the analysts.
note: Spanish "aliviar" helps you remember it.

definition: a plan or arrangement for something bad that might happen
example: We need a contingency plan in case the vendor misses the deadline.
exampleEs: Necesitamos un plan de contingencia por si el proveedor no cumple el plazo.
cloze: We need a ____ plan in case the vendor misses the deadline.
note: Used as a noun adjunct: "contingency plan", not "contingent plan".
